record.paper_title: The Flow Associated to Weakly Differentiable Vector Fields: Recent Results and Open Problems
record.context_brief: BV fields with weighted reference density
record.original_question: Assume there is a nonnegative density ρ satisfying ∂_tρ_t + ∇·(b_tρ_t)=0. When b_t belongs to BV and ρ belongs to L^∞, does one have uniqueness of the associated flow and well-posedness of the corresponding partial differential equation relative to the reference measure ρ·L^d?

evidence.quote: More generally, we may think that whenever we have a nonnegative function ρ satisfying ∂tρt + ∇ · (btρt) = 0 (3.1) then we should think to ρLd as our new reference measure and try to obtain well-posedness, at least in the regions where ρ does not vanish.
The uniqueness of the flow and the well-posedness of the PDE when bt ∈ BV and the function ρ in (3.1) belongs to L∞ are still open problems

artifact.self_contained_problem: Let $d\geq 1$ and $T>0$. Let $b:(0,T)\times\mathbb{R}^d\to\mathbb{R}^d$ be a Borel vector field with $b\in L^1((0,T);BV_{\mathrm{loc}}(\mathbb{R}^d))\cap L^\infty$. Suppose there exists a nonnegative function $\rho\in L^\infty((0,T)\times\mathbb{R}^d)$ which is a distributional solution of the continuity equation $\partial_t\rho_t+\nabla\cdot(b_t\rho_t)=0$ in $(0,T)\times\mathbb{R}^d$, so that $b$ is "nearly incompressible" with reference density $\rho$. Consider the regular Lagrangian flow $X:[0,T]\times\mathbb{R}^d\to\mathbb{R}^d$ of $b$ relative to the reference measure $\rho\,\mathcal{L}^d$, namely a Borel map satisfying $\partial_tX(t,x)=b_t(X(t,x))$ for $(\rho_0\mathcal{L}^d)$-a.e.\ $x$, with $X(0,x)=x$, and such that $X(t,\cdot)_\#(\rho_0\mathcal{L}^d)\ll\rho_t\mathcal{L}^d$. Question: Is the flow $X$ unique up to $(\rho_0\mathcal{L}^d)$-negligible sets, and is the Cauchy problem for the associated transport/continuity equation well posed relative to the reference measure $\rho\,\mathcal{L}^d$?
artifact.category_tag: Continuity equation with BV vector fields
artifact.status_search_result: The question coincides with Bressan's compactness conjecture on uniqueness of flows generated by nearly incompressible BV vector fields. It was resolved positively by S. Bianchini and P. Bonicatto, "A uniqueness result for the decomposition of vector fields in R^d" (Inventiones Mathematicae, 2020), yielding uniqueness of the regular Lagrangian flow and well-posedness of the continuity/transport equation in the L^∞ ∩ BV nearly incompressible setting.

status_evidence.title: A uniqueness result for the decomposition of vector fields in R^d
status_evidence.snippet: Bianchini and Bonicatto prove a uniqueness result for nearly incompressible BV vector fields, giving a positive answer to Bressan's compactness conjecture.
status_evidence.claim: Uniqueness of the flow and well-posedness of the continuity equation for BV b with L^∞ density rho solving the continuity equation has been established.

status_evidence.title: Bressan's Conjecture on compactness of flow for BV vector fields
status_evidence.snippet: The conjecture is implied by uniqueness of solutions to the linear transport equation for nearly incompressible BV fields, proved by Bianchini-Bonicatto.
status_evidence.claim: The uniqueness/well-posedness problem in the BV setting with L^infty density has been resolved.

status_evidence.title: Differentiability in Measure of the Flow Associated with a Nearly Incompressible BV Vector Field
status_evidence.snippet: Builds on the Bianchini-Bonicatto uniqueness theorem for nearly incompressible BV fields.
status_evidence.claim: Subsequent works treat the flow as uniquely defined, relying on the resolved uniqueness problem.
